//: Extends `expo/tsconfig.base` rather than the repo's ../../tsconfig.base.json.
That file answers to Node (module NodeNext, types: node, no JSX, no DOM) and
is right for the pure-TypeScript workspace members; this app is bundled by
Metro and renders JSX, so Expo's own base is the honest parent.
The two options the repo cares about are restated here so nothing is lost by
not extending it:
- `strict` — on everywhere in this repo.
- `erasableSyntaxOnly` — bans `enum`, `namespace` and parameter properties.
Metro's Babel transform strips types rather than compiling them, exactly
like Node >=24 does for the token generator, so those constructs would
typecheck and then fail at runtime. This is why src/config/environment.ts
is `as const` + a union instead of an `enum`.
`allowImportingTsExtensions` — @insolvia-ai/api-client has no build step and
publishes `src/index.ts` directly, with relative imports written as
`'./models.ts'` (the root tsconfig.base.json's `//allowImportingTsExtensions`
comment owns that rule and the runtime trap it avoids). The app is the first
thing to actually IMPORT that package, which pulls its source into this
program, so this program has to accept the same specifiers. Safe here for the
same reason it is safe there: Expo's base sets `noEmit`, which tsc requires
before allowing the option at all.
`moduleSuffixes: ['.native', '']` — @insolvia-ai/design-system's components
are leaf pairs re-exported as extensionless './<name>' imports. Metro
resolves those to the .native leaves on EVERY platform, web included (the
resolveRequest override in metro.config.js); this option makes tsc see the
same files, mirroring the package's own typecheck:native program. The empty
suffix stays last so ordinary imports still resolve.
